requirements.requirement: A planter (container suitable for growing plants)
requirements.evidence: Three contiguous cells (piece:-1,0,0;full, piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full) each fitted with hex-bin-full (bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-full, bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full) filled with soil via fillSoil, open-topped for light.

requirements.requirement: For a sunny kitchen windowsill (compact, low, open to sun)
requirements.evidence: Low profile 89mm tall, 478mm long x 335mm overall, open bins with no covers; joint bolts lock linear 3-cell bar that sits lengthwise on a sill. capOpenFaces applied to close outer faces, lockJoints applied. Suitable for bright kitchen sill – geometry provides full sun exposure.

fill_and_plant placed basil-young (prop:1) in bin:-1,0,0, parsley-young (prop:2) in bin:0,0,0, mint-young (prop:3) in bin:1,0,0 – three distinct herb species, young stage, each rooted in soil. Verified in look (all 3 props visible) and check_build meshClash clear with no prop warnings.

finish.summary: Built a 3-cell linear windowsill planter (478 x 335 x 89mm) with three full-depth bins filled with soil and planted with basil, parsley and mint (young plants). Open bins give full sun, low height and compact bar fits a typical kitchen sill lengthwise. House rules capOpenFaces and lockJoints applied, verified clear.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
